tasks.short: Spot training needs, prepare and give toolbox talks, demonstrate methods and equipment, record attendance and check that workers apply it.

steps.what: Supervisor spots gaps in workers' skills or safe behaviour on site
Supervisor writes toolbox talk material from scratch
Supervisor demonstrates construction methods and operation of equipment
Supervisor gives the toolbox talk on safety procedures and company policies
Supervisor keeps a paper attendance list and files it at the office
Supervisor checks that workers apply what they were taught

tasks.design: A library of standard toolbox talks per activity, kept by the safety advisor in {DOCS}, lets the supervisor pick and adapt one instead of writing it. Attendance is ticked in a checklist in the contractor's site app ({OTHER}); demonstrating, talking and checking stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Toolbox talks were written by each supervisor and attendance went on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction apps hold checklists and site forms on phones.
tasks.still_hard: A standard talk must still be made specific to this site and this crew.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a young worker how to do it right and safe, and checking the next day.

reach.task: Keep toolbox talks current after incidents
reach.learn: Whether one library keeps all sites on the same lessons.

evidence.claim: Construction software keeps site diaries, checklists and handover reports.
Names and attendance per worker are personnel data; the works council has a say in how they are recorded.

assumptions: Boundary: from spotting a need to checking practice; formal certification courses are outside.
Input contract: toolbox library kept by the company's safety advisor; crew list kept by the planner in the site app; fallback is writing talks by hand.
Safety advisor time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Demonstrating and talking do not change.
unknowns: Whether the company has a safety advisor who would keep a library.
research_questions: Do standard talks keep crews as engaged as talks written for the site?

already_counted.description: Supervisor adapts a library talk to the site.

incremental.description: Safety advisor keeps the toolbox library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most training happens by showing on site, which does not change.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk the site for clashes, call contractors and managers, attend the coordination meeting, record actions and chase them.

steps.what: Supervisor walks the site to spot clashes between trades
Supervisor phones contractors and managers to resolve problems
Supervisor attends the weekly meeting to coordinate activities of the trades
Supervisor e-mails meeting notes and an action list to all parties
Supervisor chases open actions with each contractor by phone

tasks.design: Actions from the meeting go straight into a shared action list in the project's {PROJECT} space, each with an owner, a due date and a photo of the location; owners get reminders and close actions there. Site walks, calls and the meeting itself stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Action lists were e-mailed as documents and chased by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction apps log defects and site issues with photos and assign them to parties.
tasks.still_hard: Contractors must use the shared list; problems are solved by talking.
tasks.human_edge: Getting two trades who blame each other to agree a fix on the spot.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; chasing is lighter.

reach.task: Track open site issues across projects
reach.learn: Whether shared action lists shorten time to close.

evidence.claim: Construction software keeps site diaries, checklists, handovers and defect reports.
Under the Wkb, contractors stay liable for defects found later, so open site issues need a record.

assumptions: Boundary: from spotting a problem to actions closed; contract claims are outside.
Input contract: subcontractor contacts added by the project manager to the project space; fallback is e-mail and phone.
Contractor time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Site walks, calls and meetings do not change.
unknowns: Whether subcontractors will work in the shared list.
research_questions: Do actions close faster with reminders than with phone chasing?

incremental.description: Supervisor enters actions with owner and date during the meeting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sites where contractors ignore the shared list keep phone chasing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear about a fault, inspect the machine, find the supplier or service contract, arrange repairs, reorganise the work and log the repair.

steps.what: Equipment operator reports a machine fault to the supervisor by phone
Supervisor inspects the machinery and decides on repair or replacement
Supervisor searches folders for the rental company, service contract and phone number
Supervisor phones to arrange repairs of the equipment
Supervisor rearranges the work while the machine is down
Supervisor writes the breakdown and repair in the paper machine logbook

tasks.design: An equipment register in the contractor's construction ERP ({ERP}) holds each machine with its rental company or service contract and contact; from the machine's page the supervisor sends a repair request with machine data and photo. Breakdowns and repairs log on the same page; inspecting, deciding and rearranging work stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier details sat in folders and phones, and repairs went in paper logbooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction ERP apps plan equipment from the budget and hold it per project.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent breakdowns still need a phone call; the register must be kept current.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding in minutes whether to wait, swap machines or change the day's plan.

reach.learn: Whether the register shows which machines break most.

evidence.claim: A construction ERP plans staff, subcontractors and equipment from the budget.
Work equipment must be inspected and maintained under national working conditions rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fault report to the repair logged; replacement purchases are outside.
Input contract: equipment register with contracts and contacts kept by the equipment manager; fallback is folders and phone lists.
Operator and supplier time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Inspecting and rearranging work do not change.
unknowns: Share of rented versus owned machines.
research_questions: Does machine downtime fall when repair requests carry machine data?

incremental.description: Equipment manager keeps the register current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sites with few breakdowns, or where the register is not kept, save little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect crew hours, approve them, record production and the site diary, send hours to payroll and report production weekly.

steps.what: Supervisor collects paper timesheets with each worker's hours
Supervisor checks and approves the week's personnel hours
Supervisor records production quantities on daily forms
Supervisor writes the site diary: weather, deliveries, visitors and incidents
Supervisor types approved hours into the office spreadsheet and e-mails it to payroll
Supervisor compiles weekly production reports for the project manager

tasks.design: Crew members enter their hours per project and cost code in the hours app of the construction ERP ({ERP}); the supervisor approves the week there and approved hours flow to {PAYROLL} without retyping. Production quantities and the site diary are entered on the phone in the same system, with weather filled in and photos attached, and the weekly production report is built from those records for the supervisor to check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours, quantities and the diary were written on paper and retyped into spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Construction ERP apps log hours in the app, and site apps keep diaries with photos.
tasks.still_hard: Crews must enter hours daily; hours per worker are personnel data that need works council consent.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether the recorded hours and quantities match what really happened on site.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor approves and checks instead of typing; payroll and reporting decisions stay where they were.

reach.learn: Whether approved app hours end retyping and queries.

evidence.claim: A construction ERP plans staff and equipment, logs hours in the app and turns won quotes into projects.
Construction software keeps site diaries with checklists and reports.
Names, hours and output per worker are personnel data and performance observation; the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from hours and quantities on site to reports sent; payroll processing is outside.

Input contract: hours entered daily by crew members; project and cost codes set by the project manager; payroll codes kept by the payroll administrator; production quantities entered by the supervisor; fallback is paper timesheets.
Production is recorded per crew, not per worker.
Crew and payroll time is outside the supervisor's savings.
unknowns: Whether crews have phones for hour entry.
research_questions: Do payroll corrections fall after app hours?

already_counted.description: Supervisor checks the generated production report.

incremental.description: Supervisor learns the hours and diary screens.
Crew members enter their own hours daily.

approvals.approved_version: The week's hours per worker and cost code as approved by the supervisor in s2; changes after approval need a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Crews who will not enter hours themselves leave the supervisor typing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The site supervisor keeps training, problem solving and judgement on site; timesheets, diaries and chasing move to apps.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends the day on site and closes the week's paperwork in an hour.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
